Class ZipRepacker

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.runner.build.ZipRepacker
public final class ZipRepacker extends Object
Rewrites a dependency jar so that every entry is STORED, or copies it byte for byte, and reports where each entry's data ended up.

Repacking is what the default STORED compression mode does to every dependency. It is worth the build-time cost because a stored nested entry can be handed to ClassLoader.defineClass as a slice of the memory-mapped outer archive, with no inflater and no intermediate byte[] at all.

What is preserved: entry names, their central directory order, their MS-DOS timestamps and their CRC-32 values, and the manifest, verbatim, because a per-jar manifest carries package metadata and sealing, so rewriting it would change the semantics of the classes in it. (Digest attributes left in the manifest of a jar whose signature files were dropped are inert, so they are left alone too.)

What is dropped: every extra field, including ZIP64 ones, since ZipWriter re-derives what it needs; data descriptors, because sizes are known up front and are written into the local header; the signature files of a signed jar, which cannot verify a repacked archive (ZipReader.isSignatureFile(String)); and META-INF/INDEX.LIST, which describes a class path the nested jar no longer has. ZipRepacker.RepackResult.hadSignatureFiles() tells the packager to record IndexFormat.JAR_FLAG_SIGNED_ORIGINAL.

The offsets in ZipRepacker.RepackResult.entries() are relative to the first byte of the nested jar. The packager turns them into the absolute offsets the index stores by adding the offset at which it wrote the nested jar into the outer archive, which is what ZipEntryInfo.shift(long) is for.

The nested jar itself goes wherever the caller's stream points: pass a ByteArrayOutputStream to get it as a byte array, or use repack(Path, Path) to build it in a temporary file next to the output.

1.0

    • copy

      public static ZipRepacker.RepackResult copy(ZipReader source, OutputStream target) throws IOException
      Copies an archive byte for byte, which is what the PRESERVE compression mode does: the nested jar keeps its original compression, extra fields, data descriptors, signature files and comment, and only its entry offsets have to be discovered.

      Because nothing moves, the offsets ZipReader already resolved are exactly the offsets relative to the nested jar, and are reported unchanged. Nothing is dropped, so ZipRepacker.RepackResult.droppedEntries() is empty even for a signed jar; the packager still learns from ZipRepacker.RepackResult.hadSignatureFiles() that the source was signed.

      Parameters:
      source - the archive to read; it is neither closed nor modified
      target - the stream the copy is written to; it is flushed but not closed
      Returns:
      the entries of the copy, with offsets relative to its first byte
      Throws:
      IOException - if the source cannot be read or the target cannot be written
